source.title: A Curriculum View of Robust Loss Functions

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how clean and noisy samples behave during training and evaluates test accuracy at several label-noise rates. It does not test fitting completely random labels or unstructured inputs.
record.gate_note: The paper studies loss functions and label noise. Its results on noise rates and clean/noisy sample dynamics bear on V4 and V6. It does not report random-label fitting, training-time comparisons, unstructured inputs, or regularization ablations.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares learning dynamics of clean and corrupted training samples, testing V6 with score-margin trajectories. Noise-rate sweeps also test the test-performance component of V4, but do not establish perfect training fit.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct but incomplete. The authors connect robust losses to implicit sample-weighting curricula, attribute underfitting to diminished sample weights, and show that weighting changes can alleviate it. SGD initially suppresses noisy-sample learning, robust losses can amplify this difference, and extended training or changed learning rates can substantially alter noise robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines synthetic and human label noise with several loss functions and training schedules; it does not reproduce random-label fitting or the original generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss function and training schedule affect the reported noise robustness and clean/noisy sample dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Shifting or scaling robust-loss weighting functions improves test accuracy relative to unmodified losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adjusting implicit sample weights can mitigate underfitting of robust losses.

record.problems: The clean/noisy dynamics relevant to V6 are illustrated in figures without uncertainty estimates. The reported experiments use specific datasets, architectures, and loss functions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Table 5 reports test-accuracy differences and clean/noisy weight ratios under several noise conditions, but does not measure the training-fit requirement in V4; V4 is therefore marked tested_not_extracted.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error on it, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep, the fully random-label endpoint, and joint evidence of signal capture while memorizing all corrupted labels.
The specified regularization ablations and their effects on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Completely random-label datasets and generality beyond the tested models, losses, datasets, and schedules.

missing.what: Early suppression followed by eventual noisy-sample overfitting under extended training with CE and MAE; learning-rate changes can prevent that late overfitting. Extract separate conditions without inventing unavailable curve values.

Additional clean/noisy score-margin trajectories across symmetric, human, and asymmetric noise and additional losses. Appendix C.2 explicitly reports similar trends to Figure 3; test accuracies alone are not the dynamics measure.

Unmodified AGCE on CIFAR100 has test accuracy 49.27%, 49.17%, 47.76%, 38.17%, and 16.03% across symmetric noise rates 0–0.8. Record this partial V4 measure separately from proposed-method comparisons; training fit is unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: Table 5 is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as an undeclared omission. Its best-of-five results differ from Figure 3's illustrative runs and must not be substituted for the figure captions. No verdict concerns an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels; zero or near-zero training error; test error at chance; unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The study reports test-accuracy changes under label noise but does not report training accuracy across the noise-rate sweep, so it does not establish that training fit remains perfect.
No test of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or removing regularization as described in this version.

The study measures clean/noisy sample score-margin dynamics for selected loss functions and settings, but does not test all architectures or establish a general ordering across training for arbitrary noisy or random labels.

rows.measure: The text states noisy samples improve more slowly than clean samples; the figure shows their score-margin distributions during training.
